parameters.rule: A Number List is either empty or one or more Integer Tokens separated by exactly one comma or actual line-feed Delimiter; comma and line-feed Delimiters may coexist.
parameters.subject: Number List

parameters.rule: An Integer Token is ASCII decimal digits with an optional leading minus sign, with no whitespace and no leading plus sign.
parameters.subject: Integer Token

parameters.rule: The Python interface is the importable operation add(numbers: str) -> int exposed from the string_calculator package.
parameters.subject: add(numbers: str) -> int

parameters.behavior: The command-line interface is the installed string-calculator command with one positional Number List argument and conventional stdout, stderr, and exit-status behavior defined by this specification.

parameters.rule: The product MUST export a public Python operation add(numbers: str) -> int directly from the string_calculator package interface.
parameters.subject: public Python operation add(numbers: str) -> int

parameters.rule: The Python operation MUST sum one or more supported non-negative Integer Tokens separated by supported Delimiters.
parameters.subject: Python operation

parameters.rule: The product MUST interpret leading-zero spellings by numeric value and MUST treat negative zero as zero.
parameters.subject: leading-zero spellings

parameters.outcome: raising ValueError rather than returning a partial sum
parameters.state: Number List containing one or more negative values
parameters.trigger: any parsed value is below zero

parameters.rule: For a Number List containing one or more negative values, the Python operation MUST raise ValueError whose complete message equals `negative numbers not allowed: ` followed only by every canonical negative value in encounter order, with duplicate occurrences preserved and values separated by comma and space.
parameters.subject: complete message

parameters.behavior: The product MUST install a string-calculator command accepting one supported Number List as a positional argument.
For a successful supported invocation, the command MUST write only the decimal sum and one trailing newline to standard output, write nothing to standard error, and exit zero.
For negative-number rejection, the command MUST write the exact Python error text and one trailing newline to standard error, write no sum to standard output, and exit nonzero.

parameters.expression: The command-line adapter MUST delegate to the public add operation and MUST NOT implement an independent parser or calculation path.

source_map.excerpt: A Number List is either empty or one or more Integer Tokens separated by exactly one comma or actual line-feed Delimiter; comma and line-feed Delimiters may coexist.
An Integer Token is ASCII decimal digits with an optional leading minus sign, with no whitespace and no leading plus sign.
The Python interface is the importable operation add(numbers: str) -> int exposed from the string_calculator package.
The command-line interface is the installed string-calculator command with one positional Number List argument and conventional stdout, stderr, and exit-status behavior defined by this specification.
The product MUST export a public Python operation add(numbers: str) -> int directly from the string_calculator package interface.
The Python operation MUST sum one or more supported non-negative Integer Tokens separated by supported Delimiters.
The product MUST interpret leading-zero spellings by numeric value and MUST treat negative zero as zero.
The Python operation MUST reject the entire Number List when any parsed value is below zero by raising ValueError rather than returning a partial sum.

For a Number List containing one or more negative values, the Python operation MUST raise ValueError whose complete message equals `negative numbers not allowed: ` followed only by every canonical negative value in encounter order, with duplicate occurrences preserved and values separated by comma and space.
The product MUST install a string-calculator command accepting one supported Number List as a positional argument.
For a successful supported invocation, the command MUST write only the decimal sum and one trailing newline to standard output, write nothing to standard error, and exit zero.
For negative-number rejection, the command MUST write the exact Python error text and one trailing newline to standard error, write no sum to standard output, and exit nonzero.
The command-line adapter MUST delegate to the public add operation and MUST NOT implement an independent parser or calculation path.
